title: ESP32
intro: This ESP32 acts as a gateway: it reads your RadiaCode detector's data over Bluetooth (BLE) and sends it to OpenRed over WiFi. It's not a sensor on its own, but the bridge between your RadiaCode and the internet.

betaBanner.title: Very much beta
betaBanner.body: This firmware is WiFi-only: even if your Heltec board has a LoRa radio, this build does not support LoRa/TTN yet. It works with the Heltec WiFi Kit 32 V2 (original ESP32) and V3 (ESP32-S3); the installer auto-detects which board is connected. V1 isn't supported yet.

browserBanner.title: Chrome, Edge or Opera desktop only
browserBanner.body: Browser installation uses Web Serial, an API not implemented by Safari or Firefox, and barely supported on mobile. If you can't use it, download the 4 files below and flash them with esptool from your computer.

install.heading: Install
install.description: Connect your board (ESP32 or ESP32-S3) to your computer via USB and click install. The browser will ask you to pick the serial port; the installer auto-detects which board it is and writes the right bootloader, partition table and application in one go.
install.unsupported: Your browser does not support Web Serial installation. Use Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge or Opera on desktop, or download the files and flash them with esptool.
install.notAllowed: Browser installation only works on HTTPS sites (or localhost).
install.manualFlash: If you'd rather flash by hand with esptool, pick the files for your board and their flash address (esptool.py write_flash <offset> <file>). Offsets aren't interchangeable between boards:

prereqs.heading: Before flashing, have these 3 things ready
prereqs.intro: Without them you'll get stuck halfway through the ESP32's config portal. Prepare them before touching the install button:
prereqs.item1Desc: In OpenRed, every RadiaCode is a "device", and it's not created by hand: it gets registered automatically the first time you use your RadiaCode with the mobile app, under your account. Then create a station linked to that device, with its location, in
prereqs.item1Suffix: Creating the station is not optional: without it nothing shows up on the map, even if the device is already sending data.
prereqs.item2Desc: On that same page, click "Regenerate token" on your device to get its ingest token (X-Device-Token) and save it — it's shown only once. Note: regenerating it invalidates any previous token that device was using.
prereqs.item3Desc: The ESP32 only supports 2.4 GHz networks.

manual.heading: Quick guide
manual.step1Desc: Use the install button above (or esptool by hand) to flash the ESP32.
manual.step2Desc: On first boot (or after a reset), the ESP32 opens an open WiFi network called "OPENRED-ESP32-Config". Connect to it from your phone or computer and go to http://192.168.4.1.
manual.step3Desc: Pick your WiFi network from the dropdown (or type it), its password, and paste the token from step 2 above. The upload URL is already filled in by default. Save: the ESP32 will restart and try to connect to your WiFi and, over Bluetooth, to your RadiaCode detector.
manual.reconfigure: To reconfigure WiFi or the token later: briefly press the PRG button until you reach screen 3 ("Open Portal?"), then hold it for 3 seconds to clear the configuration and reopen the portal.
